headline: Marriott International launches Project Prarambh to skill 500 youth for hospitality careers
summary: Marriott International has launched Project Prarambh in collaboration with The Job Plus and the Tourism & Hospitality Skill Council to train 500 youth across India for hospitality careers over the next two to three years. The program targets individuals aged 18 to 30 from vulnerable communities, offering technical training, workplace exposure, and mentorship to facilitate their entry into the formal workforce. This initiative aims to address India's growing demand for skilled hospitality talent while creating long-term career opportunities.

headline: V2 Retail opens 24 stores in August, adds nearly 1,000 jobs across 11 states
summary: V2 Retail opened a record 24 stores across 11 states in August, adding nearly 200,000 square feet of retail space and creating approximately 960 direct jobs. The expansion focuses primarily on Tier-II, Tier-III, and Tier-IV markets as part of the company's plan to launch 170 to 200 stores this fiscal year. The rollout is being fully funded through internal accruals and operational cash flows without equity dilution.

headline: Why succession planning is no longer replacement planning
summary: Modern succession planning is shifting from simple replacement to preparing organizations for evolving business models, regulations, and technology. Atul Mathur, EVP–HR at Aditya Birla Capital, argues that future leaders require learning agility and broad experience rather than just a position next in line. Ultimately, effective succession strategies prioritize organizational adaptability and future readiness over traditional queue-based promotions.

headline: Singapore PM’s pay rise sparks debate
summary: Singapore's Prime Minister faces public debate following an announcement that his annual compensation will rise to S$3.6 million, maintaining his position as the world's highest-paid political leader. While the government argues that high salaries attract top talent and prevent corruption, critics contend the increase exacerbates income inequality amid rising living costs. In response to concerns, the Prime Minister plans to donate the additional pay to charity over the next five years.

headline: The career decisions employees shouldn’t make in a hurry
summary: HR leaders advise employees to avoid making rushed career moves driven by peer comparison, temporary frustration, or surface-level perks like attractive titles. Instead, professionals should conduct thorough due diligence regarding an organization's actual culture and growth potential before accepting new offers. Pausing to evaluate long-term alignment helps ensure that career decisions remain beneficial even after the initial excitement fades.

headline: Rising Star: Gaurav Modak
summary: Gaurav Modak received the Rewards Guru title at the HRKatha Rising Star Leadership Awards 2025 for his expertise in compensation, performance, and incentive design. His approach highlights the importance of stakeholder ownership in reward systems, aligning metrics with strategic behavior, and transparently balancing leadership goals with employee needs.

headline: Grace period cut threatens worker security, H1B visa holders worried
summary: A proposed rule by the US Department of Homeland Security seeks to eliminate the 60-day grace period for foreign workers, including H-1B visa holders, following a job loss. Without this window to search for new employment within the country, affected professionals would be required to leave the United States immediately. The change risks causing severe personal disruption for workers while reducing flexibility and workforce stability for employers.

headline: Dilip Sinha joins Super Smelters as president & CHRO
summary: Indian steel manufacturer Super Smelters has appointed Dilip Sinha as its new President and Chief Human Resources Officer. Sinha brings extensive HR leadership experience to the role, having previously held executive positions at prominent organizations including Jindal Steel & Power, JSW Steel, Reliance Retail, and Vedanta Aluminium. His background in organizational development and talent strategy is expected to be a major asset for Super Smelters.

headline: Arun Nair is now VP-HR, IKS Health
summary: Arun Nair has been appointed as Vice President of Human Resources for the Ambulatory Business Unit at IKS Health, marking his third tenure with the healthcare technology firm. He transitions from Rubicon Research, where he led global talent acquisition and retention strategy. Nair brings extensive industry experience, having previously held senior talent acquisition and leadership roles at CitiusTech, Bellsoft Inc., and Respondez.

headline: Why being identified as a successor cannot guarantee the job
summary: Being identified as a potential successor does not guarantee a promotion, as candidate readiness and internal competition evolve over time. According to Equitas Small Finance Bank CPO Pallab Mukherji, effective succession planning must balance employee aspirations with ongoing evaluations. Consequently, organizations should maintain transparency with candidates regarding their standing and changing future requirements.

headline: Onus of vigilance clearance and APRs lies with employer, not employee: J&K and Ladakh High Court
summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh ruled that employers, rather than employees, are responsible for obtaining vigilance clearances and maintaining Annual Performance Reports (APRs). The court stated that withholding promotions, pensions, or retiral benefits due to internal administrative delays is arbitrary and violates constitutional rights. Unless active disciplinary or judicial proceedings exist, departments cannot penalize employees for administrative lapses outside their control.

headline: Flipkart tests food delivery service Eat In among Bengaluru employees
summary: Flipkart has begun internal testing of 'Eat In,' a new food delivery feature integrated within its primary app, starting with employees in Bengaluru. The company plans to expand the service to consumers following the pilot, directly entering a market currently led by Zomato and Swiggy. This launch aligns with Flipkart's broader strategy to diversify its platform offerings alongside existing verticals like Myntra and Cleartrip.

headline: Karnataka approves aerospace policy targeting Rs 60,000 crore investment, 60,000 jobs
summary: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the Aerospace Policy 2026–31, aiming to secure Rs 60,000 crore in investments and create 60,000 jobs over five years through location-based subsidies. The initiative will facilitate major manufacturing projects by defense and industrial firms while driving regional economic development. Additional approved state initiatives include a Rs 300 crore Employment Fund Programme, worker housing, an AI Hub, and a drone-testing facility.

headline: India expands healthcare workforce to improve access to specialised care
summary: India is significantly expanding its healthcare infrastructure and workforce to improve access to specialized care in rural and underserved regions. The strategy involves scaling up medical and nursing education capacity, providing financial incentives for specialist retention in difficult postings, and leveraging digital health platforms. These measures were highlighted at the WHO Regional Committee session, aligning with the newly adopted Dili Declaration to address regional healthcare shortages.

headline: Jindal (India) names Amit Khanna as chief human resources officer
summary: Jindal (India) has appointed Amit Khanna as its Chief Human Resources Officer to oversee HR and administration functions across its corporate and manufacturing operations. Khanna brings over two decades of HR leadership experience across the infrastructure, telecom, IT, and energy sectors, having previously held senior roles at organizations such as Bangalore International Airport, NTPC, and Bharti Airtel. In his new role, he will collaborate with executive leadership to drive workforce capability, organizational culture, and digital HR transformations.

headline: Beco says transparency debate will continue after Delhi HC order on HUL ads
summary: The Delhi High Court has directed eco-friendly brand Beco to remove its comparative advertising campaign targeting Hindustan Unilever's Surf Excel and Vim for exceeding permissible legal boundaries. While Beco is complying with the interim order, co-founder Aditya Ruia affirmed that the company will continue advocating for ingredient transparency and comparative advertising within the court's guardrails.

headline: Pinkvilla appoints Vivek Mohan Sharma as CEO
summary: Digital media platform Pinkvilla has appointed Vivek Mohan Sharma as its new Chief Executive Officer. Sharma brings extensive media and entertainment leadership experience, having previously served as business head at JioStar and head of branded content at Viacom18. His career also spans executive roles at Mirchi, Idea Cellular, Deutsche Bank, and ICICI Bank.

headline: Instamart turns a 25-year snack habit into a case for ‘Switch’
summary: Swiggy Instamart has launched a new marketing campaign centered on its 'Switch' proposition to encourage consumers to break habitual purchasing routines and explore alternative products. The advertisement uses a humorous story about a 25-year snack habit to show how small choices can lead buyers to healthier or higher-quality alternatives. Through this initiative, the quick-commerce service aims to drive product discovery under its promise of delivering better items at better prices.

headline: Tata Play launches Reality TV channel with Bigg Boss seasons
summary: Tata Play has partnered with Shemaroo Entertainment to launch Tata Play Reality TV, a 24x7 ad-free service dedicated to Hindi reality television. Available starting September 11, the channel will initially broadcast past seasons of Bigg Boss alongside curated short clips. Viewers can access the content on television as well as through the Tata Play mobile app.

headline: AI opens streaming TV advertising to SMBs: Amazon Ads’ Kapil Sharma
summary: Amazon Ads is leveraging AI-powered tools to make streaming TV advertising accessible to small and medium-sized businesses by significantly reducing video production costs and campaign complexity. These tools allow SMBs to rapidly generate creative assets and optimize campaigns on the same streaming inventory used by major brands. As a result, smaller advertisers are reporting higher campaign performance and increased flexibility to experiment with targeted messaging.
